Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36895: Keep witness stacks in serialized form in CScriptWitness

56fa33eac63c37513305841ff1bd73f56ad92322 doc: add release note for the reduced memory usage of witnesses (Pieter Wuille)
150002be68e0ca307b71fc968589c45d7b44687e script: store witness stacks as their serialization (Pieter Wuille)
3fca9597f0db1c7603cf9f3ab5f8081b04f60b41 span: add SameSpan (Pieter Wuille)

77f8bac8a0eec6355e3dc8252b3dcb315c242e3a test, bench, fuzz: build witness stacks before constructing a CScriptWitness (Pieter Wuille)
5fc4db08a8f4ff5af05bffe3d588600584a42534 refactor: use CScriptWitness's interface where that needs more than a rename (Pieter Wuille)
68b0ae9d9b32d3bf9c46774bccb412ddc71499e5 policy: iterate over witness stacks directly in IsWitnessStandard (Pieter Wuille)
0f1253eb5a64874fadc73ec6fdcf57247fc9ab8f script: build the witness execution stack with ToVectors() (Pieter Wuille)
0e317e2ab5d069197bf3e4c50015c890f9b14570 script: let ExecuteWitnessScript take its initial stack by value (Pieter Wuille)
e294e2812ac0d1b6fbe46ab904ef00be8e18d3ac scripted-diff: replace witnesses as a whole instead of their stack (Pieter Wuille)
ce3c41bc3e89f4dfa0ede8b4f3722cfe8a8fd3d2 scripted-diff: serialize CScriptWitness rather than its stack (Pieter Wuille)
afc3248f6b08e18aadb14ab51d36943847a229ea scripted-diff: read and compare CScriptWitness through its interface (Pieter Wuille)
a2230b147be820753ea916a18be5f986f3c141a9 scripted-diff: use CScriptWitness's size(), empty() and back() (Pieter Wuille)
4be659599837ad23da879fbafc0f323ca532fc7b test: check CScriptWitness against the vector of vectors it represents (Pieter Wuille)
fa34694a431597258039ca5e16e7f23a85e5c576 script: give CScriptWitness an interface that hides its representation (Pieter Wuille)

Pull request description:

  This is split off from #36521. This PR focuses on reducing memory usage of transactions in memory, leaving performance improvements for other PRs.

  `CScriptWitness` stores a witness stack as a `std::vector<std::vector<unsigned char>>`, which costs a 24-byte vector object and an allocation for every non-empty element. This makes it possible to construct transactions that take a large amount of memory after deserialization.

  This PR first introduces encapsulation for `CScriptWitness`, hiding its representation. The last commit then changes the representation to be single `std::unique_ptr<byte[]>` which for non-empty witness stacks stores their serialization prefixed by a small length header. Witnesses can no longer be modified in place; they can only be replaced in their entirety. Access to the individual witness stack elements is done by on-the-fly deserialization instead.

  `CScriptWitness` shrinks from 24 to 8 bytes, and `CTxIn` from 112 to 96 bytes. Worst-case allocated size for transactions kept in memory drops from roughly 28 bytes/WU to 1.6 bytes/WU.

  This worsens deserialization and validation time, adding some 50-70 ms per block to the worst case for me. A follow-up #36918 with optimizations improves the worst case deserialization time significantly instead. Other minor degradations:
  * libbitcoinkernel's witness stack element accessor becomes $\mathcal{O}(n)$ in the index of the witness element; using it to iterate a whole witness may therefore become $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$.
  * `CScriptWitness::back()` is $\mathcal{O}(n)$ in the length of the witness stack.

  Issue reported by furszy and 0xB10C.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36716: net: only monitor select exceptions while connecting

97e3c9562291f5bbc2b03fef1c70e4975eb2a8c6 net: only use the select error set while connecting (Sjors Provoost)

Pull request description:

  Alternative approach to #36688, citing the relevant parts of its description:

  > There is currently nothing preventing us to receive TCP urgent data, which would never be returned by `recv()`. Linux's `poll()` is indifferent to this, but the `select()` socket monitoring may keep reporting it as pending on some platforms.
  >
  > This would not prevent progress nor lead to a crash anymore after #36665, but it's still undesirable.

  Fix this by only adding a socket to the `select()` exception set while waiting for a non-blocking `connect()` to complete. Windows needs that to detect a failed connection. Established connections no longer monitor the exception set on any platform. This approach was suggested by theuni in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36716#issuecomment-6931290348.

  To opt in, `ErrorEvent` can now be requested from `Sock::Wait()`, like `RecvEvent` and `SendEvent`. With `select()` that adds the socket to the exception set. `ConnectToSocket()` is the only caller that requests it. There is no behavior change with `poll()`, which reports errors whether or not they are requested. Using `ErrorEvent` for this was suggested by vasild in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36716#discussion_r4692637894.

  We could instead have set `SO_OOBINLINE` on our sockets, so `recv()` returns any urgent data sent to us (and likely leads us to disconnect the peer). RFC 6093 doesn't forbid this, but the current approach seems more clear and direct to me.

  A new unit test in `sock_tests` covers the fix itself: with an urgent byte pending, waiting for `RecvEvent` must not report `ErrorEvent`. Without the fix it fails on a `select()` build.

  Backports until 29.x are straight-forward, but for 31.x and before require compensating for the scripted-diff in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/commit/f395acdeeeaa1f3fd75d3cedbf2731fa24083e9f.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#34193: wallet: make migration more robust against failures

399a5a3805884e7ac5a2cbdf616be8c9041bc2bd test: migrate a wallet with a leftover journal at its location (furszy)
42131a81fdc42ab0cb295a2267ce33e9fb8221ff test: migrate wallet located on a different filesystem (furszy)
b8ef499909b09f9dffa32172912c1e37f2e78867 wallet: migration, make sqlite creation robust against failures (furszy)
e3a5a48a03565696947be3ff3516ae013d4fd658 wallet: migration, add MigrationFilePrefix() helper (Ryan Ofsky)
b6b2f9f12b13e429a8511130bdcdc7075adbc28e wallet: use RunWithinTxn within MigrateToSQLite (furszy)
cf5e6803f07d1bfc6ae7ac655e7063c650bcb2f8 wallet: fail migration gracefully on non-writable wallets (furszy)
84a9f486475de9fab0b5cc8ab7b0338e04117163 wallet: migration, restore backup if an exception is thrown (furszy)
3a9ba874bb7efab4401d86a073964774f88de393 wallet: migration, handle exceptions during wallet creation (furszy)
edbf3b62a2cb258bb585045c769b1215c577e8e1 wallet: migration, unify watchonly and solvables wallets creation (furszy)

Pull request description:

  This is just me finding a few more edge cases after #34156 and #34176

  The goal of the PR is to handle failures in a controlled way. Just so the process can automatically restore the original wallet without requiring user manual intervention.

  The covered cases are:

  1. During `DoMigration()`: There are methods that can throw exceptions and abruptly abort the process. 
  Instead of crashing (GUI) or returning a generic exception, we now will catch and return the error gracefully. This lets the process restore the original wallet automatically.

  2. Trying to migrate a wallet in a read-only directory throws a filesystem exception and skips cleanup.
   Now the process will fail gracefully with a clear error msg, and automatically restore the original wallet.

  3. Any failure during `MigrateToSQLite` requires user manual intervention. 
  Now the original wallet db will remain untouched, and only be updated once the sqlite db creation fully succeeds.

ACKs for top commit:
  achow101:
    ACK 399a5a3805884e7ac5a2cbdf616be8c9041bc2bd
  w0xlt:
    reACK 399a5a3805884e7ac5a2cbdf616be8c9041bc2bd
  ryanofsky:
    Code review ACK 399a5a3805884e7ac5a2cbdf616be8c9041bc2bd. This is a clear improvement over master, which deletes the original database before writing the new one and asserts if anything fails after that. Now the new database is fully built before it replaces the original, failures after that point restore the backup, and a leftover journal at the wallet location stops the migration instead of corrupting the new database.

Pull request description:

  This is just me finding a few more edge cases after #34156 and #34176

  The goal of the PR is to handle failures in a controlled way. Just so the process can automatically restore the original wallet without requiring user manual intervention.

  The covered cases are:

  1. During `DoMigration()`: There are methods that can throw exceptions and abruptly abort the process. 
  Instead of crashing (GUI) or returning a generic exception, we now will catch and return the error gracefully. This lets the process restore the original wallet automatically.

  2. Trying to migrate a wallet in a read-only directory throws a filesystem exception and skips cleanup.
   Now the process will fail gracefully with a clear error msg, and automatically restore the original wallet.

  3. Any failure during `MigrateToSQLite` requires user manual intervention. 
  Now the original wallet db will remain untouched, and only be updated once the sqlite db creation fully succeeds.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35765: depends: keep local source archives in WORK_PATH

01491f22b2c77d632e8503cc446140d1ab6ccc21 depends: store local package tarballs in WORK_PATH instead of SOURCES_PATH (Ryan Ofsky)

Pull request description:

  Local package tarballs are generated from the current checkout, but depends caches them alongside downloaded archives in `SOURCES_PATH`. When checkouts share that directory, a cached local tarball can be newer than another checkout's source files, causing depends to build the wrong sources with a valid checksum and build ID.

  Store local package tarballs and their checksum stamps in `WORK_PATH/local-sources` instead. `WORK_PATH` is per-checkout by default, so generated snapshots stay with their checkout while downloaded sources remain shareable through `SOURCES_PATH`. Existing mtime-based invalidation is unchanged.

  This also handles `contrib/guix/guix-build`, which mounts each checkout at `/bitcoin`. Distinguishing local tarballs by absolute source path cannot isolate those builds when `SOURCES_PATH` is shared.

  Validation: focused checks reproduced the same-path collision with the path-hash approach and verified isolation with this change. Host/container source checksums and build IDs match; archive reuse, refresh after an edit, and downloaded-source paths were also checked. No full Guix build was run.

  Addresses #35764.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36709: guix: compute --build triplet when lowering, not at load time

d7a8360f4ef5ff90b71d87b15ec4c5048b9ea0a9 guix: compute --build triplet when lowering, not at load time (Jorge Espada)

Pull request description:

  ### Why

  `building-on` in `contrib/guix/toolchains.scm` reads `(%current-system)` once, when the module is loaded. `guix shell` loads the manifest before it applies `--system`, so the value is the system of the machine that runs the build, not the system that Guix builds for.

  So a build with `ADDITIONAL_GUIX_ENVIRONMENT_FLAGS="--system=aarch64-linux"` on an x86_64 machine (for example with `qemu-binfmt-service-type`, to get an aarch64 build machine) configures the aarch64 cross toolchain with `--build=x86_64-guix-linux-gnu`. `gcc-cross-sans-libc` then fails to configure:

  ```
  checking for CET support... configure: error: compiler and assembler with CET support are required for --enable-cet
  ```

  ### What changes

  `building-on` becomes a procedure, and its three call sites call it. Guix then computes the triplet for each derivation, under the system that the derivation is built for.

  ### How I checked

  - On master, `HOST=x86_64-linux-gnu guix shell -n --system=aarch64-linux -m contrib/guix/linux_static.scm` (with `toolchains.scm` on the load path, as `guix-build` does) gives `gcc-cross-sans-libc` with `--build=x86_64-guix-linux-gnu`. With this PR it gives `--build=aarch64-guix-linux-gnu`. That is the same derivation that `guix build -d --system=aarch64-linux` gives on master.
  - Native builds (no `--system`): the toolchain derivations from `linux_static.scm` and `manifest_gui.scm` are identical on master and with this PR. So this PR does not change release builds.
  - With this PR, an emulated aarch64 build of `x86_64-linux-gnu` on x86_64 built the whole cross toolchain and the non-GUI binaries. The GUI environment then failed in the tests of `python-pylint` (timeout under emulation) and `maturin` (snapshot mismatch). These packages have no aarch64 substitutes at the pinned Guix commit, and the failures are not related to this change.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36982: test: handle mainnet logs in `combine_logs.py`

4e1dc2e01511ef9328a54fbbf756cb8c159898a7 test: handle mainnet logs in combine_logs.py (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** Running `combine_logs.py` on the logs from a mainnet functional test such as `rpc_validateaddress.py` raises `AttributeError`. The helper expects a path like `node0/regtest/debug.log`, but mainnet writes `node0/debug.log`.

  Before #16973, the helper silently skipped the mainnet log. That PR made the search recursive, so it finds the log and then fails when the regex tries to extract a subdirectory.

  **Fix:** Get the log directory relative to `node0/` from the path the script already found.

  <details>
  <summary>Manual reproducer</summary>

  From the repository root with a functional-test build:

  ```bash
  dir=$(mktemp -d)
  build/test/functional/rpc_validateaddress.py --tmpdir="$dir/run" --nocleanup
  test/functional/combine_logs.py "$dir/run"
  ```

  The address-validation test passes. Before the fix, the last command fails in `read_logs()`:

  ```text
    File "test/functional/combine_logs.py", line 88, in read_logs
      chain = re.search(r'node0/(.+?)/debug\.log$', debug_logs[0].as_posix()).group(1)
              ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'group'
  ```

  With the fix, the same command prints both the `test` and `node0` log entries in timestamp order.
  </details>

commit.message:
net: only use the select error set while connecting

Windows uses the select() error set to report a failed non-blocking
connect(). Make ErrorEvent an event that can be requested from
Sock::Wait(), like RecvEvent and SendEvent: with select() it adds the
socket to the error set. ConnectToSocket() requests it while
connecting. This is safe on all platforms, as any error condition is
worth waking for there.

All other uses of select() now leave the error set empty. With
select(), sockets waited on without ErrorEvent no longer wake up for
or report exceptional conditions, such as TCP urgent data on an
established connection. No behavior change with poll().

Add a unit test: with an urgent byte pending, waiting for RecvEvent
must not report ErrorEvent.

Co-authored-by: Cory Fields <cory-nospam-@coryfields.com>
Co-authored-by: Vasil Dimov <vd@FreeBSD.org>
Co-authored-by: Antoine Poinsot <mail@antoinep.com>

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36950: test, bench: construct inputs/outputs declaratively in descriptor, bip352, group_outputs and ephemeral spends

5b4baa8dada19ceac2b2f882cf6ca3d071c87f87 bench: construct mempool_ephemeral_spends inputs/outputs declaratively (yuvicc)
7352a745df5dc5ee7ff11f7b4a4b4692e67603ed test: construct group_outputs_tests output declaratively (yuvicc)
73e8c18841e3195b33d1442f10dfc7b968011ffc test: construct descriptor_tests spend transaction declaratively (yuvicc)

Pull request description:

  Part of #36692.

  - `descriptor_tests`: `DoCheck` built the spending transaction with `vin.resize(1)` / `vout.resize(1)` and then wrote `nSequence` through `vin[0]`. It now uses literal `vin`/`vout` lists, which also makes the default input and the empty output visible.
  - `bip352_tests`: `bip352_p2pkh_pubkey_extraction_with_checksig_in_scriptsig` signed a transaction and then wrote the malleated scriptSig into its existing input. It is now split into an unsigned transaction used for signing and the final transaction built with the malleated scriptSig. commit.message:
doc: add release note for the reduced memory usage of witnesses

Storing witness stacks in serialized form reduces the memory that
transactions use, so the mempool can hold more of them within the
same -maxmempool limit.

script: store witness stacks as their serialization

Replace CScriptWitness's vector of vectors with a single allocation,
containing the size of the stack's serialization (4 bytes, little
endian), followed by that serialization. An empty stack uses no
allocation at all.

This means a witness stack no longer needs one allocation per non-empty
element plus one for the outer vector, and no longer has a 24-byte
overhead per element. A block whose witnesses consist of millions of
tiny elements thus no longer costs tens of bytes of memory and an
allocation per byte. It also shrinks CScriptWitness from 24 to 8 bytes,
and thus CTxIn from 112 to 96 bytes. The downside is that indexing
becomes O(n) in the distance from the bottom of the stack.

This is the simplest implementation of this representation:
deserialization still goes through a vector of vectors, and elements
are found by parsing the serialization with SpanReader and
ReadCompactSize. Both can be made faster in follow-up changes.

span: add SameSpan

Add a helper that tells whether two spans refer to the same range of
memory, rather than whether their contents are equal. A future commit
uses it to compare iterators that consist of a span.

script: remove CScriptWitness's old interface

All users of CScriptWitness now go through the interface that hides its
representation. Make the stack vector private, turning the struct into a
class, and remove IsNull() and SetNull(), which have no callers left.

The representation itself does not change here.
